case_name: Suryanarayan Sahu and Others v Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
respondent:
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
Supreme Court of India

25 November 1997
C.As. Nos. 507 and 508 of 1993 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 19 June 1989 of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Cuttack in T.A. No. 14 of 1987)
The Judgment was delivered by: Wadhwa, J.
1.  These two cross appeals arise out of the judgment dated June 19, 1989 of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Cuttack Bench (for Short, "the Tribunal" ) on a writ application filed by Suryanarayan Sahu (appellant in Civil Appeal No. 50/- of 1993) . At the relevant time, Sahu was working as a senior Draughtsman in the Regional Research Laboratory Bhubaneshwar, a unit of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). While Sahu is aggrieved by the impugned judgment in not granting him pay scale of Rs.425-700/- from 1.1.1973 as Junior Draughtsman and as senior Draughtsman in the pay scale of Rs. 550-900/- from 29.4.1974, Union of India is aggrieved as the Tribunal in the
facts: The case arises out of the judgment dated June 19, 1989 of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Cuttack Bench (for Short,
petitioner_arguments: Sahu is certainly in a better position compared to the decision of the Central Government implementing the directions of this Court in P. Savita's case as he got the scale of pay of Rs. 425-700/- from 1.8.1979.
court_reasoning: CSIR is an autonomous body. The recommendations of the Pay Commission cannot be made applicable to CSIR suo motu. It would be up to the governing body of the CSIR to adopt the recommendations of such pay Commission.
holding: The principle of classification amongst existing officers Grade-A for the purpose of fitment in the new dispensation brought about by statutory regulations could not be said to be unreasonable and arbitrary requiring to be struck down as violative of Art. 14.
Different scales of pay can be granted based on experience and merit to the employees working in the same grade. Classification based on experiences is valid.

The revised pay-scales for Draughtsmen in the CSIR are more beneficial to them than what was given in the Third Pay Commission and which recommendation had been accepted by the Central Government for its employees.
Grant of pay Scale of Rs.425-700 by the CSIR to Sahu with effect from 1.6.78 is as per the rules of the CSIR and is valid.
